question.text: The 'Quality Education DIB' referenced in Chapter 2 as an Indian example has what approximate total value, and which states does it cover?

answer.text: USD 10 million, covering Rajasthan, Gujarat and Delhi, with service providers KEF, Gyanshala and SARD.
USD 50 million, covering only Maharashtra, with a single service provider.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 2.3.1.2, 'The Quality Education DIB with a total value of USD 10 million focuses on improving literacy and numeracy of two lakh children in Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Delhi, and has multiple service providers such as KEF, Gyanshala and SARD.' The Trap: Options B, C and D all invent scale / geography numbers. Cross-Exam Context: XV (Research Analyst) treats bond-issuance sizing. X-A/X-B (IA) treats impact-bond placement to HNI donors. Assessor's Pro-Tip: The Quality Education DIB is a useful benchmark for sizing assurance engagements on education NPOs — the cost-per-beneficiary (USD 10 million / 2 lakh children = USD 50 per child) gives you a sanity check on new education DIB proposals where cost-per-beneficiary exceeds this by more than 2x.
